stem: Per Rule 150101, who appoints the Inventions and Awards Committee?

options.A: The Minister or Head of Extra-Ministerial Offices
options.D: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation

explanation: Rule 150101: the Committee is appointed by the Minister or Head of Extra-Ministerial Offices.

options.B: A representative of the Registrar of Patents and Designs
options.C: The most senior serving inventor in the MDA

explanation: Rule 150101: the Committee consists of the Chairman, Judicial or Legal Officer, and such other persons as may be appointed.

options.B: It is not published; it remains an internal document
options.D: On the website of each MDA

stem: Per Rule 150103, when do the Committee's own procedural rules come into force?

options.A: Immediately upon the Committee's first meeting
options.B: Only after they have been approved by the Minister or Head of Extra-Ministerial Offices
options.C: Only after ratification by the Federal Civil Service Commission
options.D: They never require any external approval

explanation: Rule 150103: no such rules shall come into force until approved by the Minister or Head of Extra-Ministerial Offices.

stem: Per Rule 150103, is an officer entitled to appear personally before the Committee?

options.A: Yes -- or be represented in such manner as may be approved
options.B: Only with the express permission of the Head of Government
options.C: Only if the officer is a GL.15 or above
options.D: No, all proceedings are conducted entirely in writing

explanation: Rule 150103: an Officer shall be entitled to appear personally before the Committee or be represented in such manner as may be approved.

stem: Per Rule 150104, what must an officer who has made an invention do immediately?

options.A: Report it under Secret Cover to Government through his Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office
options.B: File for a foreign patent before informing Government
options.C: Publicly announce the invention to secure priority
options.D: Sell the rights to a private company for evaluation

explanation: Rule 150104: an Officer who has made an invention must immediately report it under Secret Cover to Government through his Permanent Secretary.

options.C: The Registrar of Patents and Designs
options.D: The Inventions and Awards Committee directly, bypassing the Registrar

stem: Per Rule 150104, who decides whether an invention shall be regarded as secret?

options.A: The inventing Officer, at their own discretion
options.B: The Registrar of Patents and Designs, acting alone
options.C: The Minister or Head of Extra-Ministerial Offices

explanation: Rule 150104: the Minister or Head of Extra-Ministerial Offices shall decide as expeditiously as possible whether the invention shall be regarded as secret.

stem: Per Rule 150201, who decides whether an Officer shall be allowed controlling rights in a patent?

options.B: The officer's own Permanent Secretary, without further approval
options.C: The Registrar of Patents and Designs
options.D: The Inventions and Awards Committee, acting alone

explanation: Rule 150201: as soon as practicable, the Head of Government shall decide whether the Officer shall or shall not be allowed controlling rights in the patent.

stem: Per Rule 150201, if an invention is in all respects alien to the Officer's employment, what is he normally granted?

options.A: Only a one-time cash award, with no patent rights
options.B: No rights at all, since it falls outside his duties
options.D: Rights shared equally with the Registrar of Patents and Designs

explanation: Rule 150201: where an invention is in all respects alien to the employment of the Officer, he shall normally be granted the full rights in such invention.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 150201, pending the Head of Government's decision on controlling rights, to whom do all rights in the invention belong?

options.A: They remain legally unassigned until the patent is formally granted
options.B: They belong jointly to the Officer and the Registrar of Patents and Designs
options.C: They are deemed to belong to and be held in trust for the Government
options.D: They belong entirely and irrevocably to the inventing Officer

explanation: Rule 150201: pending the decision as to controlling rights, all rights in the invention shall be deemed to belong to and be held in trust for the Government.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 150202(a), if the Head of Government allows the Officer controlling rights in the patent, who is responsible for the expenditure of taking out the patent?

options.B: The Registrar of Patents and Designs

explanation: Rule 150202(a): the Officer shall be responsible for all expenditure in taking out the patent.

stem: Per Rule 150202(b), which of the following may the Head of Government reserve as a condition when granting controlling rights?

options.A: The right to dismiss the Officer without further process
options.B: A right of user of the invention free of royalty, and/or a share of any commercial proceeds
options.C: The right to prevent the Officer from ever being promoted
options.D: The right to reassign the patent to a foreign government

explanation: Rule 150202(b): the Head of Government may reserve a right of user free of royalty and/or a right to share of commercial proceeds.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 150202(c), may an Officer apply for an award even where Government has reserved rights under Rule 150202(b)?

options.B: Only if the reserved rights are later waived entirely
options.C: No, reserving any rights automatically disqualifies the Officer from any award
options.D: Yes -- the Officer may apply for an award whether or not any rights are reserved

explanation: Rule 150202(c): the Officer may, whether any rights are reserved under sub-paragraph (b) or not, apply to the Invention and Awards Committee for an award.

stem: Per Rule 150301, who determines whether an award shall be made and its amount?

options.A: The Head of Government, after investigation by the Invention and Awards Committee
options.B: The officer's own Permanent Secretary, without further review
options.C: The Registrar of Patents and Designs, acting alone

explanation: Rule 150301: the question of an award and its amount shall be determined by the Head of Government after investigation by the Invention and Awards Committee.

stem: Per Rule 150301(b), does reserving a royalty-free right of user to Government count against the Officer when fixing an award?

options.A: It automatically disqualifies the Officer from receiving any award at all
options.B: No -- it shall not be taken into account, unless and until Government actually exercises that right
options.C: Yes, but only for inventions made within the officer's first five years of service
options.D: Yes, it is always deducted in full from any award amount

explanation: Rule 150301(b): the reservation of a right of user free of royalty shall not be taken into account, but exercising that right is deemed a material change under Rule 150302.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 150302, if circumstances materially change after an award has already been paid, can the original decision reduce the amount already paid?

options.A: Yes, if the Committee unanimously recommends a reduction
options.B: Yes, the Head of Government may reduce it at any time without limit
options.C: No -- the amount of an award which has been paid shall not be reduced
options.D: Yes, but only by up to 50% of the original amount

explanation: Rule 150302: in any modification of the original decision, the amount of an award which has been paid shall not be reduced.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 150302, if an inventor considers a Head of Government award unacceptable, what recourse do they have?

options.A: None -- the Head of Government's decision is final and unappealable in every respect
options.B: They may apply to the Court to determine whether the award is fair remuneration under the Patents and Designs Act
options.C: They may only appeal to the Inventions and Awards Committee a second time
options.D: They must resign from the Service before pursuing any further claim

explanation: Rule 150302: where the inventor considers an award unacceptable, he may apply to the Court to determine whether it is a fair remuneration under the Patents and Designs Act.
verification_note: Independently verified against the real transcribed PSR source text by two separate reviewers with no shared context (one automated subagent, one direct cross-check against the source transcript); answer confirmed.

stem: Per Rule 150303, does this Chapter affect an Officer's duties and liabilities under the Official Secrets Act?

options.A: Yes, it fully replaces the Official Secrets Act for inventions
options.B: No -- nothing in this Chapter shall affect those duties and liabilities
options.C: It applies only to officers who have never signed the Oath of Secrecy
options.D: Yes, it suspends Official Secrets Act obligations during patent proceedings

explanation: Rule 150303: nothing in this Chapter shall affect the duties and liabilities of any Officer under the provisions of the Official Secrets Act.
